option_description: Controls whether ingress filtering rules are applied uniformly to all inbound channels — including those explicitly designated as trusted such as management interfaces, backup agents, replication links, and monitoring agents — with no carve-outs or inspection exemptions for any channel type.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires the 'ingress_filter_bypass_via_trusted_channel' exposure when this attribute is false AND at least one trusted channel type is defined. A false value means trusted channels traverse the zone boundary without content inspection, allowing external-origin malicious payloads to enter the local storage zone undetected. This is a high-criticality finding (score 8) because management and backup channels are high-value lateral movement paths.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect active firewall or iptables rules to verify whether management and backup port traffic is subject to inspection rules rather than blanket ACCEPT rules.
how_to_obtain.command: iptables -L FORWARD -v -n --line-numbers | grep -E '(ACCEPT|DROP|REJECT)' && iptables -L INPUT -v -n --line-numbers | grep -E '(management|backup|22|443|9090)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No unconditional ACCEPT rules present for trusted channel ports; all traffic passes through inspection chains before acceptance.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review WAF or proxy configuration files to confirm trusted channel source IPs or port ranges are not listed in bypass or whitelist sections that skip deep packet inspection.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No trusted channel source ranges appear in bypass or no-inspect directives; inspection applies universally.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the storage gateway or firewall management console, navigate to the ingress policy rule set and filter for rules associated with management or backup VLANs/IPs. Verify each rule has an associated inspection profile rather than a bare permit action.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Firewall Console → Policy → Security Rules → Filter by Zone: Management/Backup → Inspect 'Profile' column for each permit rule
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Every permit rule for trusted channel source zones has a non-null security profile or inspection policy attached.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the firewall or storage gateway API to retrieve all ingress rule objects and programmatically check for rules with action=permit and an empty or null inspection profile targeting trusted channel subnets.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -sk -H 'Authorization: Bearer $FW_TOKEN' 'https://<firewall-api>/api/v1/policies/security/rules?zone=trusted' | jq '.rules[] | select(.action=="permit" and (.profile == null or .profile == "")) | {name, src, dst, port}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Empty result set — no permit rules lack an associated inspection profile for trusted channel traffic.

option_description: Enumerates every channel type that has been formally granted trusted status within network policies, firewall rules, or storage platform configurations — for example management_interface, backup_agent, replication_link, or monitoring_agent.
security_impact: The Rego policy evaluates this array in combination with 'trusted_channel_ingress_filtering_enabled'. When this list is non-empty and ingress filtering is disabled, the 'ingress_filter_bypass_via_trusted_channel' exposure fires. The list itself defines the attack surface: each trusted channel type represents a potential inspection bypass path. An undocumented or over-broad trusted channel list increases risk because it widens the set of channels that may escape filtering scrutiny.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Search firewall and network policy configuration files for keywords indicating trusted or exempt channel designations, then extract and catalog each unique channel type found.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A deduplicated list of channel type labels found in policy files, which can be cross-referenced against the approved trusted channel register.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the storage platform or network orchestration API to retrieve all defined security zones or trust groups and extract the channel-type metadata associated with each.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A JSON array listing each trust group and the channel types it encompasses, enabling enumeration of all trusted channel designations.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the storage and network operations teams to obtain the authoritative list of channel types granted trusted status. Compare this against any formal CMDB or network segmentation documentation to identify undocumented trusted channels.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A reconciled list of trusted channel types that matches both operational configuration and documented policy, with any discrepancies flagged for remediation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the network policy management console, navigate to the trust zone or security zone configuration section and enumerate all zones or groups with a 'trusted' classification. Note the channel types listed within each.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Network Management Console → Zones → Security Zones → Filter: Trust Level = Trusted → Expand each zone to view member channel types
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A complete enumeration of channel types (e.g., backup_agent, management_interface) across all trusted-classified zones.

option_description: Characterizes the breadth of ingress filtering bypass granted to trusted channels — 'all' means every defined trusted channel type bypasses content inspection entirely, 'partial' means at least one trusted channel bypasses inspection while others are filtered, and 'none' means no trusted channel receives any inspection exemption.
security_impact: The Rego policy independently fires 'ingress_filter_bypass_via_trusted_channel' for both 'all' and 'partial' values, treating both as high-criticality misconfigurations (score 8). Even a partial bypass ('partial') is flagged because any single uninspected trusted channel provides a viable ingress path for attacker payloads. Only 'none' avoids this exposure. This attribute must be 'none' to prevent the rule from triggering.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Audit iptables/nftables rules to count how many trusted channel port groups have unconditional ACCEPT rules versus those routed through an inspection chain, then determine if the bypass is total or partial.
how_to_obtain.command: iptables -S | grep ACCEPT | grep -v '#' | while read rule; do echo "$rule"; done && nft list ruleset 2>/dev/null | grep -E '(accept|drop)' | grep -v '#'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: If all trusted channel ports appear in ACCEPT rules without traversing an inspection chain, scope is 'all'; if some do, scope is 'partial'; if none do, scope is 'none'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Examine WAF rule exception lists and firewall policy exception tables to identify which specific trusted channel types are listed as bypass/no-inspect exceptions.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Lines listing each trusted channel type that appears in an exception or bypass directive; count of matched types versus total trusted channel types determines scope.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review WAF or IDS logs for the past 30 days filtered by trusted channel source IPs or port ranges. The absence of any inspection log entries for a given trusted channel type is strong evidence that channel bypasses inspection entirely.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -E '(backup.agent|management.interface|replication.link)' /var/log/waf/access.log 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -20
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Non-zero inspection log entries for every trusted channel type; absence of entries for any channel type indicates it is bypassing inspection (partial or all bypass scope).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Request the ingress rule exception register from the network security team and cross-map each exception entry against the list of defined trusted channel types to determine bypass scope.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A mapping of trusted channel types to exception status — zero exceptions indicates 'none'; all types excepted indicates 'all'; subset excepted indicates 'partial'.

option_description: Indicates whether any secondary, legacy, or non-primary communication ports active on the local storage zone boundary are excluded from egress monitoring, IDS alerting, DLP coverage, or SIEM integration.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires 'egress_path_enumeration_through_unmonitored_port' when this is true AND egress enforcement mode is 'monitor_only' or 'none', and also when legacy ports are present and this is true simultaneously. An unmonitored port provides an exfiltration channel that generates no alerts and leaves no audit trail, enabling staged data theft. This is a high-criticality finding (score 8).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Generate a full list of listening and established outbound ports, then diff against the SIEM or IDS monitored port inventory to identify gaps in egress monitoring coverage.
how_to_obtain.command: ss -tunp | awk 'NR>1 {print $5}' | grep -oE '[0-9]+$' | sort -un > /tmp/active_ports.txt && echo 'Active ports:' && cat /tmp/active_ports.txt
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A list of active port numbers. Each port should be cross-referenced against the SIEM alert rule inventory; any port absent from SIEM rules is an unmonitored egress port.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Conduct an external port scan from outside the storage zone boundary and compare discovered open ports against the approved and monitored port register to identify undocumented listening ports.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Nmap output listing all open ports; any port not in the approved monitored inventory constitutes an unmonitored egress port (true value).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the SIEM for egress alert rules and extract the port list they cover, then compare against active ports to find monitoring gaps.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Ports covered by IDS/SIEM alert rules. Ports in the active set but absent from this list are unmonitored (true). Complete coverage means false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the SIEM management console, navigate to the alert rule inventory filtered by the storage zone IP range and review which destination ports have active egress detection rules, identifying any gaps.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM Console → Rules → Egress Detection Rules → Filter by Source Zone: Local Storage → Review Port Coverage column → Identify ports with 'No Rule' status
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All active ports on the storage boundary appear in the SIEM rule inventory with coverage status 'Active'. Any 'No Rule' entry confirms unmonitored egress ports are present (true).

option_description: Describes the operational enforcement posture of egress controls at the local storage zone boundary — 'enforced' means outbound traffic that violates policy is actively blocked, 'monitor_only' means violations are logged and alerted but traffic is permitted to flow, and 'none' means no egress policy is applied at all.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires 'egress_path_enumeration_through_unmonitored_port' when this is 'monitor_only' or 'none' in combination with unmonitored ports present, and also when legacy ports are in use and mode is 'none'. A 'monitor_only' posture is insufficient — it provides visibility but does not prevent exfiltration. 'none' leaves the zone completely open to unimpeded data leakage. Only 'enforced' fully prevents the high-criticality exposure (score 8).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect iptables or nftables default OUTPUT/FORWARD chain policies and explicit egress rules to determine whether the posture is ACCEPT (none), LOG-only (monitor_only), or DROP/REJECT with logging (enforced).
how_to_obtain.command: iptables -L OUTPUT -v -n --line-numbers; iptables -L FORWARD -v -n --line-numbers; iptables -P OUTPUT; iptables -P FORWARD
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Default policy ACCEPT with only LOG rules = monitor_only; default policy ACCEPT with no rules = none; explicit DROP/REJECT rules with logging = enforced.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review DLP gateway configuration to check whether the operational mode is set to block, inspect-only/alert, or passthrough for egress traffic originating from storage zone IP ranges.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Mode directive set to 'block' or 'enforce' confirms enforced; 'alert' or 'monitor' confirms monitor_only; 'passthrough' or absent confirms none.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the firewall or SD-WAN controller API to retrieve the egress policy object for the storage zone and check the enforcement action field.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON response with enforcement_mode field set to 'enforced', 'monitor_only', or 'none'; confirms the current posture directly.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Perform a controlled egress test from within the storage zone — attempt an outbound connection to a known-unauthorized destination and verify whether the connection is blocked (enforced), permitted with a log entry (monitor_only), or permitted silently (none).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Connection refused or timed out with a corresponding firewall block log = enforced; connection succeeded with a corresponding SIEM alert = monitor_only; connection succeeded silently = none.

option_description: Enumerates all port numbers or service identifiers corresponding to secondary, legacy, or non-primary communication paths currently active and listening on the local storage zone boundary — for example deprecated storage protocols, older management APIs, or decommissioned replication endpoints still running.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires 'egress_path_enumeration_through_unmonitored_port' when this array is non-empty in two conditions: when egress enforcement is 'none', and also when unmonitored egress ports are simultaneously present. Legacy ports are high-risk exfiltration vectors because they are rarely covered by modern IDS/DLP rule sets, often lack authentication hardening, and may not appear in current network diagrams. Even a single legacy port entry elevates risk significantly.

how_to_obtain.instruction: List all TCP/UDP ports currently in LISTEN state, then cross-reference against the approved current-generation port register to identify those classified as legacy or secondary.
how_to_obtain.command: ss -tlunp | awk 'NR>1 {print $5}' | grep -oE '[0-9]+$' | sort -un && netstat -tlunp 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR>2 {print $4}' | grep -oE '[0-9]+$' | sort -un
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A deduplicated list of listening port numbers. Ports not in the approved primary service list (e.g., SMBv1 port 445 where SMBv3 is standard, FTP port 21 where SFTP is standard, Telnet port 23) are legacy ports.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use nmap with service version detection to identify legacy or deprecated service versions running on non-standard or secondary ports at the storage zone boundary.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Nmap service scan output listing any open ports with legacy service identifiers such as ftp, telnet, rsh, rlogin, nfs (v2/v3), smb1, or deprecated storage protocols.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review storage service configuration files for enabled legacy protocol listeners that may activate secondary ports alongside the primary service port.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configuration entries showing legacy protocol versions enabled (e.g., min protocol = NT1 in smb.conf, or nfsvers=2 in exports) and the ports they would activate.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Request the historical port decommission log from the operations team and cross-reference against current active port scans to identify ports that were scheduled for decommission but remain active.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A list of ports marked as decommissioned in the log but still appearing in current port scans — these constitute the legacy ports in use inventory.

option_description: Indicates whether access control lists or explicit permission boundaries are actively enforced between distinct internal subzones within the local storage zone — for example between a temporary staging area, an active working set, and long-term sensitive storage — such that a process authorized for one subzone cannot freely access another.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires 'subzone_segmentation_absence' directly when this attribute is false, making it one of the primary triggers for this high-criticality exposure (score 8). Without ACL enforcement at subzone boundaries, any process or identity that gains access anywhere within the local storage zone can traverse all internal subzones freely, enabling both lateral movement and privilege escalation to higher-sensitivity data stores.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate filesystem ACLs on top-level directories representing internal subzones and verify that distinct permission sets exist between subzones rather than a uniform open permission set.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each subzone directory shows a distinct ACL with different user/group entries. If all subzones show identical or overly permissive ACLs (e.g., other::rwx), ACL enforcement is absent (false).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check storage platform-level RBAC policies for per-subzone permission assignments using the storage management CLI.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each subzone directory has a distinct owner UID/GID and differing permission bits. Uniform ownership and permissions across subzones suggests ACLs are not enforced (false).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect storage platform policy configuration files or NFS/SMB share definitions to confirm per-subzone access restrictions are declared and active.
how_to_obtain.command: cat /etc/exports 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^#' && grep -A5 '\[' /etc/samba/smb.conf 2>/dev/null | grep -E '(path|valid users|read only|browseable)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each subzone share or export entry has distinct 'valid users' or IP-restriction clauses. A single wildcard export or shared credential across all subzone paths indicates ACLs are not enforced (false).

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the storage management console or NAS web interface, navigate to the share or volume permission management section and review the ACL or permission set assigned to each subzone volume, confirming they are distinct and appropriately restricted.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Storage Management Console → Shares/Volumes → Select each subzone volume → Permissions tab → Review ACL entries per volume
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each subzone volume shows a tailored ACL with only authorized users/groups granted access. Identical ACLs across all subzone volumes or the presence of 'Everyone' with full access indicates enforcement is absent (false).

option_description: Specifies the technical mechanism used to separate internal storage subzones from each other — 'none' means no isolation exists and subzones share a flat namespace, 'logical' means isolation is implemented through directory structure or namespace conventions only without policy enforcement, and 'enforced' means isolation is backed by policy-enforced ACLs, mandatory access controls, or cryptographic boundaries.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires 'subzone_segmentation_absence' directly for 'none', and also for 'logical' when cross-subzone traversal logging is absent. 'logical' isolation (directory-level separation without policy enforcement) provides no real access barrier — a process with storage zone access can simply navigate directory paths across subzone boundaries. Only 'enforced' provides genuine isolation. This exposure is rated high criticality (score 8) because absent segmentation enables an attacker who compromises any one subzone to access all internal sensitive data stores.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Test whether a low-privilege process authorized for one subzone can read files in a different, higher-sensitivity subzone to empirically determine whether isolation is enforced or merely logical.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 'Permission denied' for both commands confirms enforced isolation. Successful listing or read access confirms isolation is only logical or absent (logical or none).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check for SELinux or AppArmor mandatory access control policies that enforce subzone isolation at the OS level, which would indicate enforced isolation beyond filesystem ACLs.
how_to_obtain.command: sestatus 2>/dev/null && semanage fcontext -l 2>/dev/null | grep -E '(storage|staging|sensitive)' || aa-status 2>/dev/null | grep -E '(storage|confined)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SELinux enabled with distinct type contexts per subzone directory (e.g., storage_staging_t vs storage_sensitive_t) or AppArmor profiles confining per-subzone access indicate enforced isolation. Disabled MAC = logical or none.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the storage architecture documentation and any network segmentation policy files to identify whether subzone separation is declared as a namespace/directory convention or as a policy-enforced boundary.
how_to_obtain.command: find /opt/storage-platform/conf/ /etc/storage/ -name '*.conf' -o -name '*.yaml' 2>/dev/null | xargs grep -lE '(subzone|segment|isolation|acl|boundary)' 2>/dev/null | head -5 | xargs grep -E '(isolation_mode|segment_type|boundary_type)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configuration entries declaring isolation_mode=enforced or boundary_type=acl confirm enforced; directory-only or namespace entries confirm logical; absent entries or isolation_mode=none confirm none.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the storage design documentation and interview the storage architecture team to determine whether subzone boundaries are implemented as directory naming conventions or as policy-enforced permission boundaries, and request evidence of policy enforcement (e.g., ACL exports, MAC policy files).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented policy enforcement artifacts (ACL export files, MAC policy definitions, cryptographic key-per-subzone evidence) confirm enforced; directory naming convention documentation only confirms logical; no documentation of any separation confirms none.

option_description: Controls whether access events that move between internal subzones within the local storage environment are captured in audit or monitoring logs. This ensures that traversal between subzones of differing sensitivity (e.g., staging versus long-term sensitive storage) is recorded for detection and forensic purposes.
security_impact: In the Rego policy, the subzone_segmentation_absence rule fires when subzone_isolation_mechanism is 'logical' AND cross_subzone_traversal_logged is false. Without this logging, logical-only segmentation provides no detective control — an attacker traversing subzones leaves no audit trail, enabling undetected lateral movement within the storage zone.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the audit logging daemon or SIEM for rules that capture subzone-crossing file or network access events. On Linux systems using auditd, check for rules targeting cross-mount or cross-partition access.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Audit rules with -w directives covering subzone mount points or -a rules capturing path traversal between labeled storage regions.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the SIEM or log aggregator configuration to verify that cross-subzone access events from storage agents are forwarded and indexed.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Input paths or log source definitions referencing storage subzone access logs with forwarding rules active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Navigate to the SIEM platform's data source inventory and confirm that storage subzone access logs appear as an active log source with recent ingestion timestamps.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM Console > Data Sources > Storage / File System Logs > Verify last event timestamp and subzone filter coverage
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Active data source entry with events ingested within the expected logging interval and subzone identifiers present in sample events.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Search historical logs for access events that indicate traversal between distinct subzone mount points or directories to confirm such events are being captured.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Log entries showing principal identity, source subzone, destination subzone, and timestamp for cross-subzone access attempts.

option_description: Determines whether session tokens or trust attributes carried by processes crossing into the local storage zone are explicitly re-evaluated and re-issued at the ingress point, rather than being accepted as-is from the external zone. When enabled, the boundary acts as an authentication checkpoint rather than a transparent passthrough.
security_impact: The Rego rule trust_propagation_via_inherited_session_context fires when session_token_revalidation_at_boundary is false AND either cross_zone_trust_inheritance_allowed is true OR boundary_ingress_monitoring_coverage is 'none'. Without revalidation, an external process can carry elevated trust into the storage zone, effectively bypassing the trust boundary — a core trust propagation leakage scenario described in the class definition.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the API gateway or zone ingress proxy configuration for token validation middleware that explicitly reissues tokens on zone entry rather than forwarding the original bearer token.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: auth_request directives or JWT validation blocks that call an internal token-exchange endpoint before proxying the request into the storage zone.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the identity provider or API gateway management API to retrieve the ingress policy applied at the storage zone boundary and check for token reissuance configuration.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON response showing tokenRevalidation: true with a reference to an internal token exchange endpoint.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the identity provider admin console, navigate to the application or service representing the local storage zone ingress and verify that token lifetime/reissuance policy is set to force re-authentication on zone crossing.
how_to_obtain.navigation: IdP Admin Console > Applications > Local Storage Zone Ingress > Authentication Policy > Session Token Reissuance on Entry
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy setting showing 'Reissue token on zone entry: Enabled' or equivalent, with no 'inherit caller session' option checked.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the platform engineering team to confirm whether the ingress handler explicitly performs a token exchange (e.g., OAuth token exchange RFC 8693) or whether it accepts the caller's existing bearer token without challenge.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented confirmation that an internal token exchange service is invoked at the zone ingress before processing any storage request.

option_description: Controls whether processes originating in the external zone are permitted to carry and exercise their existing trust attributes inside the local storage zone without undergoing re-evaluation. When set to true (allowed), the zone boundary provides no trust isolation for crossing sessions.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers trust_propagation_via_inherited_session_context when cross_zone_trust_inheritance_allowed is true AND session_token_revalidation_at_boundary is false, and also when cross_zone_trust_inheritance_allowed is true AND boundary_ingress_monitoring_coverage is 'none' or 'partial'. Allowing trust inheritance eliminates the zone boundary's enforcement value, enabling external-origin processes to operate with internal trust levels — the primary trust propagation leakage risk for this class.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review IAM policy documents and zone boundary enforcement configuration for explicit deny rules that strip or reset trust attributes (e.g., IAM condition keys, RBAC labels) on zone ingress.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Deny statements explicitly blocking trust attribute propagation from external-zone principals into local storage zone resources.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Retrieve the zone boundary enforcement policy from the policy management API and inspect whether trust inheritance is explicitly denied or permitted.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Response field crossZoneTrustInheritance: false, indicating inheritance is blocked at the boundary.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the cloud IAM or service mesh console, navigate to the local storage zone's trust policy and verify that no policy statement grants external-zone roles or service accounts direct access without attribute re-evaluation.
how_to_obtain.navigation: IAM Console > Trust Zones > Local Storage Zone > Cross-Zone Access Policy > Verify 'Inherit External Trust Attributes' is Disabled
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy showing explicit deny or absence of any allow rule that permits external-zone trust attributes to be used within the local storage zone.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check service mesh Envoy or Istio authorization policy for the storage zone to determine whether external-zone service accounts are permitted to call storage services using their existing identity context.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get authorizationpolicy -n storage-zone -o json | jq '.items[].spec.rules[].from[].source.principals'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Authorization policy sources should reference only internal-zone service accounts; presence of external-zone principals indicates trust inheritance is allowed.

option_description: Describes the completeness of monitoring and logging coverage across all ingress points into the local storage zone. Coverage levels are: 'full' (all crossing events captured including session token and trust attribute propagation), 'partial' (only some paths covered), or 'none' (no monitoring at ingress).
security_impact: This attribute is referenced by two Rego rules. For trust_propagation_via_inherited_session_context: the rule fires when session_token_revalidation_at_boundary is false AND coverage is 'none', and also when cross_zone_trust_inheritance_allowed is true AND coverage is 'none' or 'partial'. For boundary_monitoring_blind_spot_at_protocol_layer_transition: the rule considers this attribute in the broader monitoring gap analysis. Incomplete coverage creates detection-free corridors for trust propagation and lateral movement at zone ingress.

how_to_obtain.instruction: List all defined ingress points for the storage zone (firewall rules, load balancer listeners, VPC endpoints) and cross-reference against SIEM data source inventory to identify any uncovered ingress paths.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters 'Name=service-name,Values=*storage*' --query 'VpcEndpoints[].{Id:VpcEndpointId,State:State}' --output table && aws logs describe-log-groups --log-group-name-prefix /storage/ingress
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All VPC endpoints for storage services should have corresponding CloudWatch log groups with active log streams; gaps indicate partial or no coverage.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the SIEM or network monitoring platform, review the coverage map or asset inventory to verify that every identified ingress interface for the local storage zone has an active monitoring agent or log source.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM Console > Coverage Analysis > Network Zones > Local Storage Zone Ingress Points > Agent / Sensor Status
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All ingress points showing 'Monitored: Active' status. Any 'Unmonitored' or 'Stale' entries indicate partial coverage.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the IDS or network monitoring platform API to retrieve sensor deployment status for storage zone ingress network segments.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All ingress interfaces listed with status: 'active' and lastEventTime within the expected logging interval.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review audit logs to determine whether zone-crossing events, session token presentations, and trust attribute assertions at ingress are consistently recorded across all ingress paths.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Event counts across all known ingress interfaces; missing interfaces in the output indicate monitoring gaps indicating 'partial' or 'none' coverage.

option_description: Controls whether credentials (service accounts, API keys, certificates, tokens) are explicitly scoped and restricted to a single trust zone, preventing any credential valid in the external zone from also authenticating within the local storage zone. This encompasses both policy enforcement and verified absence of cross-zone credential reuse.
security_impact: The Rego rule credential_exposure_at_boundary_transition fires independently when credential_scope_isolation_enforced is false (regardless of other conditions). This makes it one of the most direct triggers in the policy — the absence of scope isolation alone is sufficient to generate a credential exposure finding. Without zone-scoped credentials, the trust boundary provides no authentication separation between zones.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the IAM or secrets management system to list service accounts or API keys and verify that each has explicit resource conditions or scope tags restricting it to either the external zone or the storage zone, but not both.
how_to_obtain.command: aws iam list-roles --query 'Roles[].{RoleName:RoleName,Arn:Arn}' --output json | xargs -I{} aws iam get-role --role-name {} --query 'Role.AssumeRolePolicyDocument' | jq 'select(.Statement[].Condition.StringEquals["aws:RequestedRegion"] != null)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All storage-zone roles contain condition keys that restrict them to internal zone resource ARNs; no role appears in both external-zone and storage-zone resource policies.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect secret management configuration (e.g., HashiCorp Vault policies) to verify that storage-zone secrets are bound to internal-zone authentication paths and external-zone paths cannot access them.
how_to_obtain.command: vault policy read storage-zone-policy | grep -E '(path|capabilities|allowed_policies)' && vault policy read external-zone-policy | grep -E '(path|capabilities)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: storage-zone-policy grants access only to storage/* paths; external-zone-policy has no overlap with storage/* paths, confirming scope isolation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Search access logs for authentication events where the same principal identity or credential subject appears in successful authentications against both external-zone and storage-zone resources.
how_to_obtain.command: grep 'AUTH_SUCCESS' /var/log/storage-zone/access.log | awk '{print $7}' | sort > /tmp/storage_principals.txt && grep 'AUTH_SUCCESS' /var/log/external-zone/access.log | awk '{print $7}' | sort > /tmp/external_principals.txt && comm -12 /tmp/storage_principals.txt /tmp/external_principals.txt
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Empty output from comm indicating no shared principal identities between zones; any output indicates credential scope isolation is not enforced.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the cloud IAM console or identity provider, filter credentials by their allowed resource scope and confirm no credential appears in both external-zone and local-storage-zone resource permission sets.
how_to_obtain.navigation: IAM Console > Service Accounts > Filter by Resource Scope > Compare External Zone Accounts vs Storage Zone Accounts > Check for Overlap
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Disjoint sets of service accounts with no account appearing in both zone permission assignments.

option_description: Indicates whether a single credential store (e.g., a secrets manager, identity provider, or certificate authority) is used to issue and manage credentials for both external-zone and local-storage-zone access without zone-specific access restrictions on the store itself. A shared store without zone partitioning allows any entity that can read from the store to obtain credentials for either zone.
security_impact: The Rego rule credential_exposure_at_boundary_transition fires when shared_credential_store_across_zones is true AND zone_boundary_credential_reuse_detected is true. A shared credential store is a structural prerequisite for cross-zone credential misuse — it centralizes risk such that compromise of external-zone access to the store immediately threatens local storage zone authentication integrity.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the secrets management platform to identify whether separate secret paths, namespaces, or engines are used for external-zone versus storage-zone credentials, or whether a single undifferentiated store serves both.
how_to_obtain.command: vault secrets list -detailed | grep -E '(external|storage|zone)' && vault kv list secret/ | grep -E '(external|storage|internal)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Distinct secret engine mounts or namespaces (e.g., 'external-zone/' and 'storage-zone/') with separate access policies; a single 'secret/' path serving all zones indicates a shared store.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the identity provider or API gateway configuration to determine whether a single credential issuer endpoint serves authentication requests from both external and storage zone service consumers.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Separate issuer endpoints or audience restrictions for each zone; a single issuer with no audience differentiation indicates a shared credential store.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the secrets management or identity provider console, navigate to the credential store inventory and check whether zone-specific namespaces, access tiers, or policy boundaries exist between external and storage zone credentials.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Secrets Manager Console > Namespaces / Engines > Verify separate namespaces for 'external-zone' and 'local-storage-zone' with non-overlapping IAM access policies
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Two distinct namespaces or engines, each with access policies referencing only their respective zone's service accounts.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the secrets management or platform team to determine whether a unified credential store was intentionally designed to serve both zones, and whether zone-specific policy partitions exist within that store.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documentation showing either separate credential stores per zone or, if shared, explicit access control policies within the store that prevent cross-zone credential retrieval.

option_description: Records whether evidence exists — from audit logs, access records, or configuration analysis — that the same credential (principal identity, token subject, certificate, or API key) has successfully authenticated in both the external zone and the local storage zone. This is a detection-oriented attribute reflecting observed behavior rather than policy intent.
security_impact: Combined with shared_credential_store_across_zones, this attribute directly triggers the credential_exposure_at_boundary_transition Rego rule. A true value for both attributes confirms that the trust boundary has already been violated in practice — not merely that it is theoretically possible. This represents an active credential exposure condition requiring immediate remediation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Correlate authentication success events across external-zone and storage-zone access logs to identify any principal subject, client certificate CN, or API key ID that appears in both.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Empty output indicating no credential has been used in both zones; any output lines confirm zone_boundary_credential_reuse_detected should be set to true.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the SIEM or log analytics platform for cross-zone authentication correlation — searching for the same token subject or service account name appearing in both zone authentication logs within a defined time window.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SIEM_TOKEN' https://siem.internal/api/v1/search -d '{"query":"event.action:auth_success AND zone:(external-zone AND local-storage-zone) GROUP BY user.id","timerange":"30d"}' | jq '.hits[] | select(.doc_count > 1)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Zero results indicating no credential authenticated in both zones; results with doc_count > 1 across zones confirm credential reuse.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For certificate-based authentication, extract subject CNs from TLS access logs for both zones and find intersections indicating the same certificate was presented to services in both zones.
how_to_obtain.command: grep 'SSL_CLIENT_S_DN' /var/log/nginx/external-zone-ssl.log | awk '{print $NF}' | sort -u > /tmp/ext_certs.txt && grep 'SSL_CLIENT_S_DN' /var/log/nginx/storage-zone-ssl.log | awk '{print $NF}' | sort -u > /tmp/stor_certs.txt && comm -12 /tmp/ext_certs.txt /tmp/stor_certs.txt
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Empty comm output; any certificate CN appearing in both files indicates cross-zone certificate reuse.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the cloud provider's CloudTrail or activity log console, filter for the same IAM role or user ARN appearing in successful API calls targeting both external-zone resources and storage-zone resources.
how_to_obtain.navigation: CloudTrail Console > Event History > Filter by: Event Type = AwsApiCall, Username = [suspected shared principal] > Check resource ARN patterns for both zone prefixes
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Events for the principal should appear only against resources within one zone; presence of storage-zone resource ARNs alongside external-zone ARNs confirms credential reuse.

option_description: Indicates whether monitoring or logging agents are explicitly deployed and configured at points where network-layer traffic is translated into file-system operations or inter-process communication (IPC) — for example, where NFS/SMB network requests are translated to POSIX filesystem calls, or where HTTP API calls are translated to named pipe or socket IPC. These translation points represent the actual zone crossing location in many storage architectures.
security_impact: The Rego rule boundary_monitoring_blind_spot_at_protocol_layer_transition fires independently when protocol_translation_points_monitored is false, making this a standalone trigger regardless of other configuration. It also fires when zone_crossing_alert_coverage is 'partial' AND protocol_translation_points_monitored is false. Protocol translation points are a known blind spot — monitoring placed only at the network layer misses activity that occurs after protocol conversion, creating a detection gap at the actual zone boundary crossing.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Identify active protocol translation processes (NFS daemon, Samba, FUSE mounts, named pipes) and verify that eBPF probes, auditd rules, or logging agents are attached to them.
how_to_obtain.command: ps aux | grep -E '(nfsd|smbd|fuse|rpcbind)' | grep -v grep && auditctl -l | grep -E '(nfs|smb|fuse|fifo|pipe)' && bpftool prog list | grep -E '(vfs|file|socket)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Translation processes have corresponding auditd watches or eBPF programs attached; absence of any matching auditd or bpftool entries for active translation processes indicates unmonitored points.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the monitoring agent configuration (e.g., Falco, Sysdig, Auditbeat) to verify that file-system and IPC syscall probes are enabled and scoped to cover protocol translation service processes.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Falco rules or auditbeat modules referencing translation-layer syscalls (open, read, write triggered by network-facing daemons); absence indicates no coverage at protocol translation points.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the monitoring platform's agent inventory API to retrieve sensor deployment topology and confirm coverage at identified protocol translation host interfaces.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each protocol translation host shows active probes with monitored_protocols including the relevant translation protocol (nfs, smb, ipc); empty or missing entries indicate unmonitored translation points.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Perform a controlled test file operation through the protocol translation layer (e.g., write a file over NFS) and verify that a corresponding log entry appears in both the network-layer and file-system-layer monitoring systems within the expected detection window.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The test file write appears in both network-audit.log (as an NFS WRITE operation) and fs-audit.log (as a VFS write event); absence from either log confirms a monitoring gap at the protocol translation point.

option_description: Controls the extent to which SIEM/IDS alerting rules are configured to trigger on zone-crossing events specifically at protocol-layer transition points into local storage (e.g., where network-layer traffic translates to filesystem or IPC operations).
security_impact: The Rego policy fires the 'boundary_monitoring_blind_spot_at_protocol_layer_transition' exposure when this value is 'none', or when it is 'partial' and protocol translation points are also unmonitored. Without full coverage, attackers can traverse the zone boundary at protocol translation seams without generating any alerts, creating a detection blind spot for lateral movement and data exfiltration.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query your SIEM (e.g., Splunk) for existing correlation rules that reference protocol translation events such as SMB-to-NFS gateway events, iSCSI handoffs, or NFS mount operations to enumerate rule coverage.
how_to_obtain.command: splunk search 'index=_internal sourcetype=splunk_audit | search title=*zone* OR title=*crossing* OR title=*protocol_translation* | table title, enabled' -auth admin:password
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A list of rule titles indicating which protocol translation points are covered; absence of entries indicates 'none' coverage.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In your SIEM console (e.g., Elastic SIEM, Microsoft Sentinel), navigate to Detection Rules and filter by tags or rule names referencing 'zone crossing', 'protocol translation', 'NFS', 'SMB gateway', or 'iSCSI'. Assess whether all known translation points have corresponding rules.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM Console → Detection Rules → Filter by tag: zone_crossing OR protocol_translation → Review enabled rules
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A complete list of enabled rules covering every protocol translation ingress/egress point; gaps indicate 'partial' or 'none'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the IDS rule set files (e.g., Suricata or Snort rule files) to identify rules explicitly matching zone-boundary protocol transition traffic patterns such as NFS mount requests or SMB session initiation at the storage boundary.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Matching rule lines for each relevant protocol; no matches indicate 'none' coverage.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review recent IDS/SIEM alert logs to determine whether any alerts were generated for protocol-layer transition events at the storage boundary. Absence of such alert categories in historical logs strongly suggests 'none' or 'partial' coverage.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Alert entries referencing zone-crossing protocol events; no entries suggest coverage gaps.

option_description: Controls whether the shared boundary interface or API gateway enforces per-entity (per-client or per-tenant) namespacing and scoped routing, ensuring that one external entity cannot access storage paths or internal zones intended for another entity.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers the 'lateral_movement_via_shared_boundary_interface' exposure when this is false and internal zones are reachable from the shared interface. Without per-entity segmentation, a compromised external entity can enumerate or access storage paths belonging to other entities, enabling unauthorized data access and lateral movement across tenant boundaries.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the API gateway configuration (e.g., Kong, NGINX, AWS API Gateway) to verify whether route definitions or upstream proxy rules include per-client namespace prefixes, tenant ID path parameters, or scoped ACL policies.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configuration entries showing per-tenant or per-client route scoping; absence indicates segmentation is not enforced.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the API gateway management API to retrieve route and plugin configurations, then verify that each consumer or client is bound to a namespace-restricted route and cannot access routes outside their assigned scope.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Routes with path prefixes or tags scoped per entity (e.g., '/tenant-a/', '/client-b/'); shared or wildcard paths indicate missing segmentation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the API gateway management console (e.g., Kong Manager, AWS API Gateway Console), review each API route for consumer restrictions, resource policies, or usage plan bindings that limit access to per-entity paths.
how_to_obtain.navigation: API Gateway Console → APIs → Select Boundary API → Routes → Inspect each route for consumer restrictions or namespace bindings
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each route shows a consumer group or namespace restriction; routes accessible to all consumers indicate missing per-entity segmentation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Using test credentials for Entity A, attempt to access a storage path known to belong to Entity B through the shared API. A properly segmented API should return 403 Forbidden or 404 Not Found.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: HTTP 403 or 404 response indicating access is denied; HTTP 200 indicates segmentation is absent.

option_description: Describes the authentication and authorization model enforced at the shared boundary interface for external entities, ranging from unauthenticated ('none') to unique credentials with enforced scope restrictions ('entity_scoped').
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers 'lateral_movement_via_shared_boundary_interface' when this value is 'none' or 'shared_credential' and internal zones are reachable from the shared interface. Weak access control models allow attackers to impersonate other entities or use a single compromised credential to access all entity zones, eliminating effective boundary enforcement.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the API gateway or boundary proxy authentication plugin configuration to determine whether authentication is disabled, uses a single shared API key, uses per-entity unique keys without scope, or uses per-entity keys with enforced scope restrictions.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Plugin entries showing authentication type; 'anonymous' or a single shared key value indicates weak models; per-consumer JWT with scope claims indicates 'entity_scoped'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the API gateway for its consumer and authentication plugin configurations to determine whether each consumer has a unique credential and whether scope restrictions are bound to those credentials.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s http://localhost:8001/consumers | jq '.data[] | {username: .username}' && curl -s http://localhost:8001/plugins | jq '.data[] | select(.name=="jwt" or .name=="key-auth" or .name=="oauth2") | {name: .name, config: .config}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Multiple consumers each with unique credentials and scope-limiting plugin config indicate 'entity_scoped'; a single shared key or no auth plugin indicates 'shared_credential' or 'none'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the storage platform administrator to determine the access control design. Ask specifically: Are all external entities using the same API key? Does each entity have a unique credential? Are credentials bound to specific storage path scopes?
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Responses confirming unique scoped credentials per entity indicate 'entity_scoped'; shared credentials indicate 'shared_credential'; no authentication indicates 'none'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the API gateway management console, inspect the authentication plugin attached to the boundary API and review consumer bindings to determine whether scope restrictions are applied per consumer.
how_to_obtain.navigation: API Gateway Console → APIs → Boundary API → Plugins → Authentication Plugin → Consumers → Review scope or ACL bindings per consumer
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each consumer has distinct credentials with ACL or scope restrictions indicating 'entity_scoped'; shared or absent restrictions indicate weaker models.

option_description: Indicates whether the routing and forwarding rules behind the shared boundary interface allow traversal to internal storage zones or subzones beyond the immediate boundary, effectively permitting deep zone penetration through the shared API path.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers 'lateral_movement_via_shared_boundary_interface' when this is true in combination with missing per-entity segmentation or weak access control. Reachability of internal zones from the shared interface means that any entity (or attacker) using the interface can potentially pivot from the boundary to sensitive internal storage subzones not intended for external access.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the API gateway or reverse proxy upstream configuration to identify whether any routes proxy or forward requests to internal storage subzone addresses (RFC 1918 ranges, internal hostnames, or mount paths beyond the boundary layer).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Upstream entries pointing to internal RFC 1918 addresses beyond the boundary node indicate internal zones are reachable; only boundary-local addresses indicate they are not.

how_to_obtain.instruction: From the shared boundary interface's network segment, attempt to reach internal storage subzone IP addresses or hostnames (e.g., internal NFS server, internal database storage node) using traceroute or curl to determine whether routing permits traversal.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Traceroute completing to internal storage IPs or HTTP responses other than connection timeout indicate internal zones are reachable.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect firewall or security group rules governing traffic from the shared boundary interface to internal storage subzone network segments to determine whether any rules permit forwarding.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ACCEPT rules permitting forwarding from the boundary interface subnet to internal storage subnets indicate reachability; only DROP/REJECT rules indicate proper isolation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In your cloud provider or firewall management console, review security group or network ACL rules for the shared boundary interface to identify inbound/outbound rules permitting traffic to internal storage zone subnets.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Cloud Console → VPC → Security Groups → Select Boundary API Security Group → Outbound Rules → Check for rules targeting internal storage subnet CIDRs
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Outbound rules permitting TCP to internal storage subnets indicate internal zones are reachable; no such rules indicate proper boundary isolation.

option_description: Controls whether rate limiting or bandwidth/volume throttling mechanisms are actively enforced at the storage zone boundary to restrict how quickly or how much data can leave the local storage environment.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers 'insufficient_egress_rate_limiting_enabling_staged_exfiltration' when this is false and either egress volume thresholds are unconfigured or anomaly detection is absent. Without rate limiting, an attacker can exfiltrate data at a slow, steady pace that avoids triggering volume-based alerts while remaining within normal operational patterns, enabling prolonged undetected staged exfiltration.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect storage gateway, firewall, or proxy configuration files for egress rate limiting directives such as traffic shaping, QoS policies, or bandwidth cap definitions applied at the storage zone egress interface.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Directives such as 'limit_rate', 'rate_limit', or 'bandwidth' with defined values indicate rate limiting is enabled; absence indicates it is not.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check Linux traffic control (tc) rules on the storage zone egress network interface to determine whether queuing disciplines or rate limits are applied.
how_to_obtain.command: tc qdisc show dev eth0 && tc class show dev eth0 && tc filter show dev eth0
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output showing 'tbf' (token bucket filter), 'htb', or 'sfq' qdiscs with rate parameters indicates rate limiting is active; 'pfifo_fast' only indicates no rate limiting.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In your firewall or network policy management console (e.g., pfSense, Palo Alto, AWS Network Firewall), navigate to the egress policy for the storage zone interface and check for traffic shaping or rate limiting rules.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Firewall Console → Policies → Egress Rules → Storage Zone Outbound → Traffic Shaping / Rate Limiting → Review active policies
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Active rate limiting rules with defined byte/bandwidth thresholds on the storage egress path; absence of such rules indicates the control is disabled.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query your cloud provider's API for network ACL or security group egress rules that include rate limiting annotations, or query a storage gateway service for its bandwidth throttling configuration.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Response showing 'AverageUploadRateLimitInBitsPerSec' or 'AverageDownloadRateLimitInBitsPerSec' with non-zero values indicates rate limiting is enabled.

option_description: Controls whether a maximum data egress volume threshold is defined in SIEM, DLP, or network monitoring tooling such that alerts are generated or traffic is automatically blocked when cumulative data transfer volume exceeds the defined limit.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers 'insufficient_egress_rate_limiting_enabling_staged_exfiltration' when this is false and either rate limiting is disabled or anomaly detection is absent. Without a volume threshold, attackers can extract arbitrarily large datasets incrementally without any volume-based detection, as no upper bound exists to trigger defensive action.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In your DLP platform (e.g., Microsoft Purview, Symantec DLP, Forcepoint), navigate to policy definitions and locate any policies targeting the local storage zone with data volume thresholds that trigger alerts or blocks on egress.
how_to_obtain.navigation: DLP Console → Policies → Data Transfer Policies → Filter by Source: Local Storage Zone → Review threshold conditions
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policies with defined volume thresholds (e.g., 'alert if > 500MB transferred in 1 hour') indicate the control is configured; no such policies indicate it is absent.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query your SIEM's REST API to retrieve alert rules or correlation searches that contain volume-based conditions for egress traffic from the storage zone.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Search entries with volume threshold conditions (e.g., 'bytes_out > 524288000') referencing the storage zone indicate the threshold is configured.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect network monitoring tool configuration files (e.g., Zeek scripts, ntopng alerts, NetFlow analyzer thresholds) for defined volume-based egress alert thresholds associated with the storage zone subnet.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configuration lines defining volume thresholds tied to egress alerts; absence indicates no volume threshold is configured.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the SOC or network security team to determine whether any formal volume threshold policy exists for the storage zone egress, and whether it is documented, enforced, and tested.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Confirmation of a documented, actively enforced volume threshold with evidence of test alerts indicates the control is configured; lack of documentation or awareness indicates it is absent.

option_description: Controls whether a UEBA, IDS, or network analytics solution is actively baselining and alerting on deviations in egress traffic volume, frequency, or destination patterns at the storage zone boundary to flag statistically unusual data transfers.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers 'insufficient_egress_rate_limiting_enabling_staged_exfiltration' when this is false and either rate limiting or volume thresholds are also absent. Behavioral anomaly detection provides a compensating control when absolute thresholds are not triggered, detecting slow-and-low exfiltration that deviates from established baselines even if it stays under static volume caps.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In your UEBA platform (e.g., Splunk UBA, Microsoft Sentinel UEBA, Exabeam) or network analytics tool, verify that a behavioral baseline model exists for egress traffic from the local storage zone, and that deviation alerts are active and assigned to an analyst queue.
how_to_obtain.navigation: UEBA Console → Models → Data Egress / Network Exfiltration Models → Filter by Asset: Storage Zone → Verify model status is 'Active' and alert rules are enabled
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An active model with a training baseline and enabled alert rules for the storage zone egress path indicates anomaly detection is enabled.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query your network analytics or SIEM API to check whether anomaly detection policies or machine learning jobs are configured and running for the storage zone egress traffic.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer TOKEN' 'https://sentinel.azure.com/workspaces/<workspace-id>/providers/Microsoft.SecurityInsights/alertRules?api-version=2021-10-01' | jq '.value[] | select(.kind=="MLBehaviorAnalytics" or .kind=="Anomaly") | {name: .name, status: .properties.enabled}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Alert rule entries with 'enabled: true' and type 'MLBehaviorAnalytics' or 'Anomaly' referencing network egress indicate anomaly detection is active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify whether a local intrusion detection or network monitoring agent (e.g., Zeek, Suricata with threshold rules, OSSEC) is running on the storage zone boundary host and has anomaly detection modules loaded.
how_to_obtain.command: systemctl status suricata zeek ossec 2>/dev/null; suricata --list-runmodes 2>/dev/null | grep -i anomaly; zeekctl status 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Running service status and loaded anomaly detection modules indicate egress anomaly detection is active at the host level.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review recent UEBA or IDS alert logs to determine whether any egress anomaly alerts have been generated for the storage zone. Recent alerts (even low-severity) confirm the detection system is operational and baselining.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Log entries with anomaly alert types referencing storage zone egress activity confirm detection is enabled and functioning; absence may indicate detection is disabled or not yet triggered.

option_description: Controls whether a scheduled and enforced audit process exists that periodically inventories all mount points, symlinked paths, attached storage paths, and accessible directories within the local storage zone boundary to detect unauthorized additions.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers 'zone_boundary_definition_drift' when this is false in combination with unapproved mounts being present or boundary controls not being applied to new mounts. Without regular boundary audits, new mount points or symlinked paths added over time can silently expand the zone's attack surface, introducing uncontrolled ingress/egress points that lack the original boundary controls and are invisible to defenders.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the system's cron jobs, systemd timers, or scheduled task configurations to determine whether a recurring mount point inventory or boundary audit script is scheduled.
how_to_obtain.command: crontab -l 2>/dev/null; systemctl list-timers --all | grep -iE '(audit|mount|boundary|storage.scan)'; ls -la /etc/cron.d/ /etc/cron.daily/ | grep -iE '(audit|mount|storage)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Scheduled entries referencing mount audits or boundary scans with a defined recurrence interval indicate the audit is enabled; no entries indicate it is absent.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the current mount table and compare it against any documented baseline or approved mount inventory file to identify whether a comparison mechanism exists.
how_to_obtain.command: cat /proc/mounts | awk '{print $1, $2, $3}' | sort > /tmp/current_mounts.txt; diff /tmp/current_mounts.txt /etc/approved_mounts_baseline.txt 2>/dev/null || echo 'No baseline file found - audit not configured'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A diff showing only approved mounts with no extra entries, and the existence of a baseline file, confirms auditing is active; 'No baseline file found' confirms it is absent.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the storage administrator to determine whether a formal mount point and storage boundary audit process exists, what its frequency is, who is responsible, and where audit results are recorded.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Confirmation of a documented recurring audit procedure with evidence of recent audit results (logs, tickets, or reports) indicates the control is enabled; inability to produce evidence indicates it is absent.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review system audit logs or SIEM events for periodic mount inventory events, boundary definition checks, or automated alerts triggered by new mount detection tools such as auditd or a custom monitoring script.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Audit log entries showing periodic mount inventory events or new-mount detection alerts confirm the audit is active; absence of such entries indicates the control is not implemented.

option_description: Tracks the number of mount points or attached paths currently active in the local storage zone that are not listed in the approved boundary definition baseline. A non-zero value indicates zone boundary drift where uncontrolled ingress/egress points may have been introduced without applying required boundary controls.
security_impact: The Rego policy for zone_boundary_definition_drift fires when unapproved_mount_count > 0 combined with either storage_boundary_audit_enabled being false or boundary_controls_applied_to_new_mounts being false. Each unapproved mount represents an unvetted ingress/egress point that bypasses the original zone boundary controls, enabling data exfiltration paths or lateral movement footholds that were never reviewed for compliance.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Linux, enumerate all currently active mounts and compare against your approved baseline list. Export active mounts to a file and diff against the approved inventory.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An integer representing the count of active mounts not found in the approved baseline. A result of 0 indicates no drift.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Windows, list all mounted volumes and drives using PowerShell and cross-reference against a stored approved baseline inventory file.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-PSDrive -PSProvider FileSystem | Select-Object Name,Root | Compare-Object -ReferenceObject (Import-Csv C:\baseline\approved_mounts.csv) -DifferenceObject (Get-PSDrive -PSProvider FileSystem | Select-Object Name,Root) -Property Name | Where-Object {$_.SideIndicator -eq '=>'} | Measure-Object | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Count
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Integer count of mounts present on the system but absent from the approved baseline CSV. Zero means no unapproved mounts.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the infrastructure-as-code repository (e.g., Terraform state or Ansible inventory) to enumerate all declared storage mounts, then compare to what is observed live on the host to detect out-of-band additions.
how_to_obtain.command: terraform state list | grep 'mount\|volume\|disk' | sort > /tmp/iac_mounts.txt && findmnt -rno TARGET | sort > /tmp/live_mounts.txt && diff /tmp/iac_mounts.txt /tmp/live_mounts.txt
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Diff output showing lines present in live_mounts.txt but not in iac_mounts.txt indicates unapproved mounts. No output means full alignment.

how_to_obtain.instruction: If the host is managed by a cloud provider or storage orchestration platform (e.g., AWS, Azure, Kubernetes), query the management API to retrieve attached volumes and compare against the approved asset inventory.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: List of volume IDs attached to the instance. Cross-reference each ID against the approved inventory. Any ID not in the approved list increments the unapproved count.

option_description: Indicates whether ingress/egress filtering and access controls equivalent to those applied to the original zone boundary are automatically enforced on any newly added mount points or attached storage paths. When false, new mounts are added to the zone without inheriting the required boundary enforcement controls.
security_impact: The Rego zone_boundary_definition_drift policy fires when boundary_controls_applied_to_new_mounts is false in combination with unapproved_mount_count > 0 or storage_boundary_audit_enabled being false. Without automatic control inheritance, each new mount point becomes a gap in the boundary enforcement layer — a storage path that is logically inside the zone but lacks the access restrictions, filtering rules, and monitoring coverage applied to the original boundary definition, enabling unauthorized data ingress or exfiltration.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the storage provisioning automation configuration (e.g., Ansible playbooks, Terraform modules, or cloud-init scripts) to determine if boundary security controls (ACLs, mount options such as noexec/nosuid/nodev, and audit rules) are declared as mandatory dependencies for all new mount resources.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Mount definitions should include security mount options and reference audit rule tasks. Absence of these patterns in mount provisioning tasks indicates controls are not automatically applied.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Linux, inspect /etc/fstab and systemd mount unit files to verify all mount definitions include security-hardening options, indicating controls are applied at provisioning time rather than post-hoc.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Any mount entry returned lacks the baseline security options (noexec, nosuid, nodev). An empty result means all declared mounts include required options.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the storage or infrastructure team to determine whether the mount provisioning runbook or infrastructure-as-code pipeline includes a mandatory security controls checklist or automated policy gate that blocks deployment of mounts without boundary controls.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A documented procedure or pipeline gate that explicitly validates boundary control assignment before a new mount is activated. Absence of such a gate means the attribute value is false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In cloud environments using AWS Systems Manager or Azure Policy, navigate to the policy compliance dashboard and check for policies that enforce volume/mount tagging or security group assignment, indicating controls are applied automatically.
how_to_obtain.navigation: AWS Console > AWS Config > Rules > Search for 'ec2-volume-inuse-check' and custom boundary-control rules; or Azure Portal > Policy > Compliance > Filter by storage-related initiatives
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Compliant status for all storage resources indicates boundary controls are enforced at provisioning. Non-compliant resources indicate automatic control application is not in place.

option_description: Indicates whether physical storage ports (USB, eSATA, Thunderbolt, FireWire) and removable media interfaces on the local storage host are disabled at the firmware level, restricted via OS device management policy, or physically secured with port blockers to prevent unauthorized device attachment.
security_impact: The Rego boundary_control_bypass_via_physical_interface policy fires directly when physical_port_access_controls_enabled is false. Physical interfaces bypass the entire logical ingress/egress enforcement layer — an attacker with brief physical access can attach a device and read or write zone data without triggering any network-layer boundary controls. This is classified as a direct exposure trigger regardless of other control states.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Access the system BIOS/UEFI firmware settings during boot to inspect USB and external port configuration. Look for settings labeled 'USB Configuration', 'External Ports', or 'I/O Interface Security' and verify they are set to disabled or locked.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Reboot system > Press BIOS key (F2/F10/Del/Esc depending on manufacturer) > Advanced Settings > USB Configuration or I/O Interface Security > Verify USB ports show 'Disabled' or 'Locked'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All external port entries should display 'Disabled', 'Locked', or 'User Password Required'. Any entry showing 'Enabled' or 'Available' indicates physical_port_access_controls_enabled is false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Windows, use PowerShell to check the USB device installation policy in the registry and Group Policy, which controls whether USB storage devices can be connected.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\USBSTOR' -Name Start | Select-Object Start; Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceInstall\Restrictions' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
how_to_obtain.expected_output: USBSTOR Start value of 4 (disabled) indicates USB storage is blocked at the driver level. Value of 3 means enabled. DeviceInstall Restrictions keys confirm GPO-level control.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Linux, check if USB storage module is blacklisted and verify udev rules that block or restrict removable storage device attachment.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A blacklist entry for usb-storage in /etc/modprobe.d/ confirms kernel-level blocking. Relevant udev rules restricting block device attachment confirm OS-level port access controls are active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review endpoint security or UEM platform configuration (e.g., Microsoft Intune, CrowdStrike Falcon Device Control, Symantec DCS) policy export to verify device control policies are applied to the host and set to block or restrict physical storage interfaces.
how_to_obtain.command: Get-MgDeviceManagementDeviceConfiguration | Where-Object {$_.DisplayName -like '*device control*' -or $_.DisplayName -like '*USB*'} | Select-Object DisplayName, Id
how_to_obtain.navigation: Microsoft Intune Admin Center > Devices > Configuration Profiles > Filter by 'Device Control' or 'Endpoint Security > Attack Surface Reduction'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An assigned, active device control policy targeting the host with USB/removable media set to 'Block' or 'AuditBlock' confirms physical port access controls are enabled.

option_description: Defines the operating system-level policy governing whether removable media (USB drives, external HDDs, SD cards, optical media) can be mounted on the local storage host. The three possible states are: blocked (mounting is prevented entirely), require_authorization (mounting requires explicit approval or privileged action), or allow_all (any user may mount any removable device without restriction).
security_impact: The Rego boundary_control_bypass_via_physical_interface policy fires unconditionally when removable_media_mount_policy is 'allow_all', and also fires when it is 'require_authorization' but physical_interface_activity_logged is false. The allow_all state provides a trivially exploitable data exfiltration and introduction path that completely bypasses logical boundary controls. The require_authorization state without logging creates an unmonitored physical access vector where authorized mounting cannot be audited for abuse.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Linux, check udisks2 and polkit configuration to determine the current removable media automount policy for non-root users.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -r 'org.freedesktop.udisks2' /etc/polkit-1/rules.d/ /usr/share/polkit-1/rules.d/ 2>/dev/null; gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.media-handling automount 2>/dev/null; cat /etc/udev/rules.d/*usb* 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Polkit rules returning 'polkit.Result.NO' for udisks2 mount actions indicate 'blocked'. Rules requiring authentication map to 'require_authorization'. Default permissive rules or no rules indicate 'allow_all'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Windows, query Group Policy and registry settings that control AutoPlay and removable storage device access policies.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: RemovableStorageDevices policy with Deny_All set to 1 maps to 'blocked'. Presence of specific class deny keys without full block indicates 'require_authorization'. Absence of all keys maps to 'allow_all'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Microsoft Intune or a comparable UEM, navigate to the device control or attack surface reduction policies to view the current removable media mounting policy applied to the host.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Microsoft Intune > Endpoint Security > Attack Surface Reduction > Device Control Policy > Review 'Removable Storage' settings for the assigned policy group
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy entry showing 'Block' for removable storage access maps to 'blocked'. 'Audit' maps to 'require_authorization' with logging. No policy or 'Allow' maps to 'allow_all'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Linux systems using USBGuard, review the active rule set to determine if removable device mounting is blocked or conditionally permitted based on device authorization.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ImplicitPolicyTarget of 'block' with no permissive rules indicates 'blocked'. Specific allow rules with logging indicate 'require_authorization'. ImplicitPolicyTarget of 'allow' or usbguard not installed indicates 'allow_all'.

option_description: Indicates whether attachment and access events on physical storage interfaces (USB device connect/disconnect, removable media mount/unmount, direct-attached storage activity) are captured in system audit logs. Without this logging, physical interface use is invisible to security monitoring, creating a detection gap at one of the most direct data exfiltration paths.
security_impact: The Rego boundary_control_bypass_via_physical_interface policy fires when removable_media_mount_policy is 'require_authorization' but physical_interface_activity_logged is false. Even with an authorization requirement, the absence of logging means there is no record of who mounted what device and when, eliminating accountability and making it impossible to detect abuse of authorized access or investigate incidents involving removable media. This gap enables undetected data introduction or exfiltration via physical interfaces.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Linux, verify that auditd rules are configured to capture USB device attachment events (kernel module loads) and block device access events.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Active auditctl rules watching for usb or block device events confirm logging is enabled. Absence of any matching rules indicates physical_interface_activity_logged is false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Windows, verify that audit policy is configured to log Plug and Play events (Event ID 6416) and object access events for removable storage (Event ID 4663), which together cover physical interface activity.
how_to_obtain.command: auditpol /get /subcategory:'Plug and Play Events' /subcategory:'Removable Storage'; Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[EventID=6416]]" -MaxEvents 5 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object TimeCreated, Message
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Auditpol showing 'Success and Failure' for Plug and Play Events and Removable Storage confirms logging is active. 'No Auditing' for either subcategory indicates the attribute is false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review recent system logs for evidence of physical device attachment events to confirm that logging infrastructure is actively capturing these events in real time.
how_to_obtain.command: journalctl -k | grep -iE 'usb|scsi|block device|new.*storage' | tail -20; dmesg | grep -iE 'usb|new.*storage' | tail -20
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Kernel log entries timestamped with USB or block device attachment events confirm the OS is generating log data. Absence of any such entries even after a known device attachment indicates logging gaps.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check endpoint detection and response (EDR) platform or SIEM for configured detection rules targeting USB and removable media events to verify physical interface activity is being ingested and monitored.
how_to_obtain.navigation: CrowdStrike Falcon > Event Search > Search for 'RemovableMediaConnected' OR 'DeviceControlPolicy'; OR SIEM Console > Detection Rules > Filter by 'usb' or 'removable media' to confirm active ingestion rules
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Active detection rules with recent event data for USB/removable media attachment events confirm physical_interface_activity_logged is true. No relevant rules or zero recent events indicate logging is not occurring.
